### Harold Jansen

unread,

May 1, 1996, 12:00:00 AM5/1/96

to

I just got El Grande and I've read through the rules, but I have a couple   
of quick questions before I try a game.

1) This is probably an easy one. Can power cards be re-used? In other   
words, do you start each of the nine rounds with the full set of thirteen   
cards? I think the answer to this is yes, but I want to check to make   
sure.

2) In the first part of a player's turn when you're moving caballeros from  
the provinces to the yard, the translation I have (from The Game Cabinet)   
says that if the provinces are empty, you have to remove the missing  
caballeros from the board. These caballeros are removed from the game,  
presumably never to be used again as punishment for not keeping sufficient  
caballeros in the provinces. The translation has a translator's note that   
the translation of this rule may be wrong. My question is: is the way I've   
described it correct?

Thanks in advance for any answers to these questions. This game looks   
great: beautiful components.

Harold Jansen

### Brian Bankler

unread,

May 1, 1996, 12:00:00 AM5/1/96

to

Harold Jansen wrote:  
>   
> I just got El Grande and I've read through the rules, but I have a couple  
> of quick questions before I try a game.  
>   
> 1) This is probably an easy one. Can power cards be re-used? In other  
> words, do you start each of the nine rounds with the full set of thirteen  
> cards? I think the answer to this is yes, but I want to check to make  
> sure.

NO. You use each auction card once. Even if this isn't  
explicit in the rules, the "Get a used auction card back" card from  
the #4 pile makes that implicit.

> 2) In the first part of a player's turn when you're moving caballeros from  
> the provinces to the yard, the translation I have (from The Game Cabinet)  
> says that if the provinces are empty, you have to remove the missing  
> caballeros from the board. These caballeros are removed from the game,  
> presumably never to be used again as punishment for not keeping sufficient  
> caballeros in the provinces. The translation has a translator's note that  
> the translation of this rule may be wrong. My question is: is the way I've  
> described it correct?

Although I have no evidence to the contrary, I have to believe  
this is incorrect. But, since I have no evidence, that's all i can say  
about it, except to quote the translation. (Reader's of german are,  
as always, invited to correct my statements).  
 Ken's Translation, incidentally, says you "MAY" remove   
caballeros from the board to add to the provinces. I suspect that  
this might be right. But you are never forced to remove people from  
the board. Also note the preceeding sentence in the rules "Move  
AT MOST the number of Caballeros shown on the power card..."  
(Emphasis mine). I think you just read must in for may.

> Thanks in advance for any answers to these questions. This game looks  
> great: beautiful components.  
>   
> Harold Jansen

### Chris Lawson

unread,

May 1, 1996, 12:00:00 AM5/1/96

to

Harold Jansen (hja...@gpu3.srv.ualberta.ca) wrote:  
: I just got El Grande and I've read through the rules, but I have a couple   
: of quick questions before I try a game.

: 1) This is probably an easy one. Can power cards be re-used? In other   
: words, do you start each of the nine rounds with the full set of thirteen   
: cards? I think the answer to this is yes, but I want to check to make   
: sure.

Once you start playing you will see why the answer to this is no (with an  
exception). Power cards are discarded once used not to be used again (unless  
you get the card with the special use of picking up one of your discarded  
power cards). The use of the 1 and 13 power cards are very important to  
the timing of your plays (to maximise scoring opportunities), so keeping  
track of who has played them can be useful (and to a lesser extent, the 2  
and 12 power cards).

: 2) In the first part of a player's turn when you're moving caballeros from

: the provinces to the yard, the translation I have (from The Game Cabinet)   
: says that if the provinces are empty, you have to remove the missing  
: caballeros from the board. These caballeros are removed from the game,  
: presumably never to be used again as punishment for not keeping sufficient  
: caballeros in the provinces. The translation has a translator's note that   
: the translation of this rule may be wrong. My question is: is the way I've   
: described it correct?

I do not remember this rule but I am not sure you have it right, this might  
be due to the fact I have misunderstood your understanding of the rule.  
The way I remember it is that if you run out of Caballeros from the  
provinces then you have no more available to you, I do not know of a time  
when any are removed from the game. There are times when Caballeros are   
removed from board and returned to the Provinces.

Hope that helps. El Grande is a good game, expensive but good.

Chris Lawson  
c.r.l...@bra0108.wins.icl.co.uk

### Tom Affinito

unread,

May 1, 1996, 12:00:00 AM5/1/96

to

I believe the Game Cabinet rules have two errors.

Firstly, the section you note where Ken says "I'm not sure sure the rule  
is right". This section heading makes it clear in the German that Power  
cards are discarded once played. [With the exception of that Special  
Action that lets you take a Power Card back] Cabelleros can be removed  
from the board when the provinces are empty, and this feature is an am  
important one. The translation is wrong when it implys that cabelleros are  
removed from the game, and this is why Ken put his editorial comment in.  
It is Power cards that are removed from the game.

Secondly, one of the Special Action cards is not translated. It is the  
card that has an arrow pointing to the first scoring position of a region  
[I believe it's a 3 pointer Special Action card], and it means that all  
regions should be scored , but only the first place is awarded points. [By  
normal interpolation, if there's a tie for first, those people would score  
the second value, which is assumed to be zero in this case...ie, no one  
scores on a tie in this case] If you look over your cards with the German  
rules and the Game Cabinet translation, you'll see this card that they  
miss.

Great game, and of course thanks always to the Cabinet for their work!!

--   
Tom Affinito  
ta...@apsu.org

Thanks to everyone for the quick answers.

Going through the rules more carefully again, I found the action card  
which said you take your power card back out of the discard pile and  
realized I was wrong in my initial impression.

Thanks also for the clarifications on the other rules. It didn't make   
sense to me that they would be removed from the game.

And while I'm thanking people, I'd also like to echo the thanks of a   
previous poster who thanked the Game Cabinet people for all of their work.   
It's quickly become my favorite web page. I've been checking every day for   
the next update.

Harold Jansen

I'm no expert, but I'd say Blue wouldn't have to move any. The King's Region  
being off-limits is one of those absolute rules. It seems that the case is  
so specific, that the advantages blue gets for the first turn (and it's not  
even a scoring round) makes for very little difference at all. Besides Blue  
should try to spread out a little more anyway...
